Captivity of Zedekiah and the People Foretold for Their Disobedience and Perfidy.</title> <div sID="gen18476" type="x-p"/> The prophecy (<reference osisRef="Jer.34.1-Jer.34.7">Jr 34:1-7</reference>) as to Zedekiah is an amplification of that in <reference osisRef="Jer.32.1-Jer.32.5">Jr 32:1-5</reference>, in consequence of which Jeremiah was then shut up in the court of the prison. The prophecy (<reference osisRef="Jer.34.8-Jer.34.22">Jr 34:8-22</reference>) refers to the Jews, who, afraid of the capture of the city, had, in obedience to the law, granted freedom to their servants at the end of seven years, but on the intermission of the siege forced them back into bondage.<div eID="gen18476" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18477" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10354"/><hi type="bold">1. Jerusalem and ... all the cities thereof--</hi>(see on <reference osisRef="Jer.19.15">Jr 19:15</reference>). It was amazing blindness in the king, that, in such a desperate position, he should reject admonition. <div eID="gen18477" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10362"/><div sID="gen18488" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10362"/>13. The last year of Zedekiah was the sabbatical year. How just the retribution, that they who, against God's law and their own covenant, enslaved their brethren, should be doomed to bondage themselves: and that the bond-servants should enjoy the sabbatical freedom at the hands of the foe (<reference osisRef="Jer.52.16">Jr 52:16</reference>) which their own countrymen denied them! <div eID="gen18488" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10363"/><div sID="gen18489" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10363"/><hi type="bold">14. At the end of seven years--</hi>that is, not on the eighth year, but within the limit of the seventh year, not later than the end of the seventh year (<reference osisRef="Exod.21.2">Ex 21:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Exod.23.10">23:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.15.12">De 15:12</reference>). So "at the end of three years" (<reference osisRef="Deut.14.28">De 14:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.18.10">2Ki 18:10</reference>), and "after three days, I will rise again" (<reference osisRef="Matt.27.63">Mt 27:63</reference>), that is, on the third day (compare <reference osisRef="Matt.27.64">Mt 27:64</reference>). <div eID="gen18489" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 14. At the end of seven years-- that is, not on the eighth year, but within the limit of the seventh year, not later than the end of the seventh year ( Ex 21:2 ; 23:10 ; De 15:12 ). So "at the end of three years" ( De 14:28 ; 2Ki 18:10 ), and "after three days, I will rise again" ( Mt 27:63 ), that is, on the third day (compare Mt 27:64 ).
entries.reader_content_plain: 14. At the end of seven years-- that is, not on the eighth year, but within the limit of the seventh year, not later than the end of the seventh year ( Ex 21:2 ; 23:10 ; De 15:12 ). So "at the end of three years" ( De 14:28 ; 2Ki 18:10 ), and "after three days, I will rise again" ( Mt 27:63 ), that is, on the third day (compare Mt 27:64 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10366"/><div sID="gen18492" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10366"/><hi type="bold">17. not ... proclaiming liberty--</hi>Though the Jews had ostensibly emancipated their bond-servants, they virtually did not do so by revoking the liberty which they had granted. God looks not to outward appearances, but to the sincere intention.<div eID="gen18492" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18493" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I proclaim a liberty--</hi>retribution answering to the offense (<reference osisRef="Matt.7.2">Mt 7:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.18.32">18:32</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.18.33">33</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gal.6.7">Ga 6:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jas.2.13">Jas 2:13</reference>). The Jews who would not give liberty to their brethren shall themselves receive "a liberty" calamitous to them. God will manumit them from His happy and safe service (<reference osisRef="Ps.121.3">Psa 121:3</reference>), which is real "liberty" (<reference osisRef="Ps.119.45">Psa 119:45</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.8.36">Joh 8:36</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.3.17">2Co 3:17</reference>), only to pass under the terrible bondage of other taskmasters, the "sword," &c.<div eID="gen18493" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18494" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">to be removed--</hi>The Hebrew expresses agitation (see on <reference osisRef="Jer.15.4">Jr 15:4</reference>). Compare <reference osisRef="Deut.28.25">De 28:25</reference>, 48, 64, 65, as to the restless agitation of the Jews in their ceaseless removals from place to place in their dispersion. <div eID="gen18494" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 17. not ... proclaiming liberty-- Though the Jews had ostensibly emancipated their bond-servants, they virtually did not do so by revoking the liberty which they had granted. God looks not to outward appearances, but to the sincere intention. I proclaim a liberty-- retribution answering to the offense ( Mt 7:2 ; 18:32 , 33 ; Ga 6:7 ; Jas 2:13 ). The Jews who would not give liberty to their brethren shall themselves receive "a liberty" calamitous to them. God will manumit them from His happy and safe service ( Psa 121:3 ), which is real "liberty" ( Psa 119:45 ; Joh 8:36 ; 2Co 3:17 ), only to pass under the terrible bondage of other taskmasters, the "sword," &c. to be removed-- The Hebrew expresses agitation (see on Jr 15:4 ). Compare De 28:25 , 48, 64, 65, as to the restless agitation of the Jews in their ceaseless removals from place to place in their dispersion.

Compare De 28:25 , 48, 64, 65, as to the restless agitation of the Jews in their ceaseless removals from place to place in their dispersion.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10367"/><div sID="gen18495" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10367"/><hi type="bold">18. passed between the parts thereof--</hi>The contracting parties in the "covenant" (not here the law in general, but their covenant made before God in His house to emancipate their slaves, <reference osisRef="Jer.34.8">Jr 34:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.34.9">9</reference>) passed through the parts of the animal cut in two, implying that they prayed so to be cut in sunder (<reference osisRef="Matt.24.51">Mt 24:51</reference>; Greek, "cut in two") if they should break the covenant (<reference osisRef="Gen.15.10">Ge 15:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.15.17">17</reference>). <div eID="gen18495" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 18. passed between the parts thereof-- The contracting parties in the "covenant" (not here the law in general, but their covenant made before God in His house to emancipate their slaves, Jr 34:8 , 9 ) passed through the parts of the animal cut in two, implying that they prayed so to be cut in sunder ( Mt 24:51 ; Greek, "cut in two") if they should break the covenant ( Ge 15:10 , 17 ).
